messages:
From: Emily Rhodes <emily@avalonhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary priority pool for May launch

Hi Laura —

Hope you’re well. Quick ask from our ops team as we firm up timelines for our product launch (internal name: Avalon Live). We expect a 48–72 hour launch spike and want to avoid client-visible throttling or dropped requests. The traffic plan I’m attaching estimates up to 3x our normal token consumption during peak hours.

Specifics:
- Target window: 2027-05-10 00:00 UTC -> 2027-05-12 00:00 UTC (48 hours, may extend to 72h depending on adoption)
- Peak profile: short bursts of high concurrency (200–300 rps) with large response lengths (avg. 220 tokens)
- Current plan: hosted Redwood API (self-serve) — we do not have Dedicated today

Can Redwood provide a temporary priority token pool / elevated rate limits for that window (we understand this is an exception to fairness policies)? If so, please outline: approval steps, expected cost, any telemetry/SLAs you need from us, and timing to sign an amendment.

We’re happy to prepay an uplift if that’s required. Attaching our traffic plan for reference.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Rhodes
Head of Ops, Avalon Health
emily@avalonhealth.com

Attachment: avalon_launch_traffic_plan.pdf

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Emily Rhodes <emily@avalonhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary priority pool for May launch

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the traffic plan — looks clear. We can support a short-term elevated lane but it’s an exception to our hosted fairness policy, so there are a few required items before we flip the switch:

1) Signed amendment (term: temporary priority pool) that specifies the window and tokens/hour cap.
2) Prepayment of the uplift estimate or a card on file to cover overage.
3) A brief telemetry hook (a shared Drive doc or webhook) so our SREs can pull tail-latency metrics in real time during the window.

Operationally we can provision a "priority token pool" that isolates N tokens/h from the general fairness pool and routes requests through an elevated path. For an initial proposal: 9 million tokens/hour pool during peak hours (configurable) for 48 hours, with automatic rollback after the window.

Prelim cost estimate: ~$32k for a 48-hour window at the proposed size (will refine after product signs off on rate sizing). This includes priority routing, short-term elevated compute, and SRE on-call.

I’ve looped Marissa (Customer Success/demos) and Ben (Growth sales) so we can coordinate a quick approval + DocuSign. If you can confirm the final window and whether you want an optional 24h buffer (72h total), we’ll prepare an amendment and a one-line invoice.

— Laura

Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Avalon priority pool request (details + ask)

Team —

Forwarding Avalon’s request (see Emily’s note below). Quick analysis and proposed approach:

- Customer: Avalon Health (mid-market, live product, no Dedicated)
- Request: temporary priority token pool to avoid fairness throttling during a 48–72h launch window
- Proposed technical config: provision a carved-out priority pool of 9M tokens/hour, with a fail-open fallback that drops to 2M tokens/hour to avoid global impact. Route policy: tag requests from Avalon and route to elevated kernel queue; KV cache stays shared.
- Risk: during sustained full consumption we’ll see added tail-latency risk for the host pool; risk mitigations: SRE on-call + short-lived autoscaling bump.

Cost estimate (back-of-envelope):
- Compute & priority routing: $22,500
- SRE on-call & monitoring: $6,500
- Admin/billing + amendment processing: $3,000
Total: ~$32,000 for 48h (rounded).

Asks:
1) Ben — commercial signoff on the price and that we can invoice/prebill.
2) Marissa — CS to commit to an SRE runbook and the telemetry share during the window.
3) Soojin — legal review on short-term amendment; minimal indemnity tweaks only.

If we green-light, I’ll send a formal DocuSign amendment and we’ll schedule a pre-launch runbook call.

Thanks — L

Quick read — this is fine with a couple small asks:

1) Amendment needs a one-paragraph statement that this is a temporary service exception and that all normal fairness/rate-limit policies resume at window close.
2) We should require a telemetry SLA from Avalon: access to a shared dashboard or daily tail-latency report during the window. This reduces operational ambiguity.
3) Limit liability: absolute liability cap tied to the uplift fee (standard practice).

If Ben approves the pricing and Finance can create a one-line invoice / prepay link, legal can sign off ASAP. No need for extended review.
